title: No frame of a 50 track zoom is held up by the system's drawing cleanup
goal: Zooming the timeline of a 50 track edit is smooth but for a rare single frame, about one in 3,000, that takes 20 to 58 milliseconds and reads as a tiny hitch. Every frame of a zoom should be as smooth as the rest.
notes: Split off an-edit-with-50-tracks-and-100-clips-scrolls-pla (its acceptance: what is not reached is filed, one cost each). Measure: a walk with setup {"forget":["all"],"wideEdit":50}, wait 3, then {"do":"speed","measure":"timeline","form":"long"} six times and {"do":"wait","seconds":90,"onTheClock":true}; profile it with Scripts/perf/pass-profile.sh <walk> then Scripts/perf/pass-profile.py /tmp/photonz-pass-sampler --waits. Caught 2026-11-25, two of two: 'PASS 139 zoom out held | 38.9' and 'PASS 576 near fit fresh | 31.6'. Main thread: CA::Transaction::run_commit_handlers -> _dispatch_sync_f_slow on RenderBox's queue (27 looks of the first on CoreAnimation's own mutex in CA::Context::commit_transaction). Holder in both, a dispatch worker: RB::SharedSurfaceGroup::prune_removed_locked -> test_markers -> RB::CommitMarker::Observer::test_displayed -> -[CAContext waitForCommitId:timeout:] -> CA::Context::ping / wait_for_synchronize -> mach_msg, 27 to 36 ms, that is the window server. No app code on it. The only lead: that cleanup runs when drawings that share a surface (RBLayer, SwiftUI Canvas and drawn text) go away or change size, so fewer drawings coming and going in a zoom (held paintings as plain CGImage layers, no Canvas) should mean fewer cleanups. Not tried.
acceptance: Over ten runs of the timeline measure on the 50 track edit (about 17,000 frames), no frame holds the main thread over 16 ms (today: 21 ms once, 33 ms once, 58 ms once in eleven runs, unprofiled)
No change in what the timeline draws: film of a zoom in, out and near Fit before and after, opened and compared, none blank
Zoom and scroll p95 stay under 8.3 ms and the edits under 16 ms in Scripts/perf/speed-walk.sh --wide 50
If the hold cannot be avoided from the app, the audit says so with what was tried, and the task is dropped with that rather than worked round at a cost a person would see

Audit under queue/audits/ with before and after numbers. Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not

Pass 1 (2026-11-26). Reproduced: ten timeline measures (17,040 frames), long frames 40.2/38.9/40.3 ms (zoom) and 20.9/19.1 (scroll). Profiled (pass-profile --waits): main thread in run_commit_handlers waiting on RenderBox's queue or in CABackingStoreSynchronize/CA::Context mutex, while a RenderBox worker (prune_removed_locked -> test_markers -> waitForCommitId) or main itself (RBLayer add_subsurface -> wait_for_allocations) waits 27-36 ms on the window server. WindowServer at 45% CPU with the probe not running.

Built a probe-only layer census (Sources/Photonz/Playtest/LayerCensus.swift; touch /tmp/photonz-layer-census/on): per measure, drawn layers added/removed/resized, each drawn layer's displays, and every -[CAContext waitForCommitId:timeout:] (swizzled), with main-thread ones put down to the layer displaying. Pass 3 (2026-11-27). Ten runs on main first: the first zoom frame from Fit was already 7.5-14.6 ms (no change aimed at it; pass 2's 16-21 did not reproduce), but a scroll frame around the 17th of each run was 12.2-17.1 ms. Profiled with pass-profile (others threshold lowered to 8 ms for one run, put back): the commit waited in -[_SwiftUIProxyImage finish] for CA::Render::copy_image -> RB::ImageProvider::wait_phase, while RenderBox drew a lane picture and converted every clip thumbnail in it on the CPU (RB::TextureCache::prepare_cgimage -> CGContextDrawImage, colour conversion from the recording's space). Fix: ClipFilmstripFrames.finish keeps each thumbnail as 8 bit BGRA in sRGB (PictureReadyToDraw, PhotonzRender, tested). After, ten runs: worst 15.8 ms (zoom in frame 1), scroll worst 10.9; speed walk --wide 50 p95 6.5/6.9/6.4/5.2, edits 7-13 ms.

Chose converting the thumbnails once over converting each lane picture into the display's colours because the latter forced the drawing onto the main thread (1.6-5 ms a picture, p95 6.4 -> 10-13 ms) and off the main thread for late pictures it changed nothing measurable; both tried, the second taken out. Pictures: stills at Fit identical (0.001 mean), 258 filmed frames none blank. Walks run: the three recording walks that read thumbnails (a-recording-replaced-on-disk..., a-recording-replaced-while-open..., exporting-over-the-open-recording...) all ok. Not checked: whether the hour-long timeline's 30 ms frame (triage note) was the same wait; its lanes draw thumbnails too, so it may be. Left rough, no task: the first zoom frame from Fit (SwiftUI graph, up to 15.8 ms) is the nearest frame to the bar.
